findings.summary: Inter-Recipe truncation attack against DropBundle is undetectable — direct inter-Node analog of F3's intra-Node total_chunks defense is missing.
evidence: crates/benten-drop/src/envelope_sig.rs:90-93 — `build_envelope_message` clones the bundle then zeroes `envelope_sig`, `issuer_verifying_key`, AND `content` BEFORE signing. So the envelope-sig binds ONLY the header (version + mode + spec_cid + audience + auth_grant + restricted_spec + per_node_attestation).

crates/benten-drop/src/bundle.rs:282-313 DropBundle struct — there is NO `content.len()` / `total_recipes_count` / `expected_recipe_count` field. `content_count()` accessor at L317 returns `self.content.len()` (the OBSERVED count, not a signed count).

Reproducer: producer builds bundle with 5 Recipes, signs envelope. Attacker takes the wire bytes, drops `content[2..]` (keeps 2 Recipes), re-encodes. envelope-sig STILL verifies (header bytes unchanged). grant-binding-sig STILL verifies (unchanged). AEAD on the 2 remaining Recipes STILL verifies (intra-Node AAD intact). Recipient receives 2 Recipes, believing they got all the Recipes the issuer intended.

F3 ratification (per the retraction of G-CORE-9 R1 triage Fork 1) was EXPLICITLY about closing the truncation attack at the chunk level — `aad_per_chunk` now binds `total_chunks` so an attacker who slices a 10-chunk ciphertext to 5 chunks cannot fabricate matching tags. The same threat-model class at the Drop bundle composition layer (slicing a 5-Recipe bundle to 2 Recipes) is UNCLOSED.

This is the direct sibling-finding the coordinator follow-up named: 'Audit ALL chunked-AEAD call sites for same-attack-class on OTHER AAD-bound fields ... per-Node CID? two-CID mapping integrity?' — extended to the Drop bundle composition layer (which IS the per-Node-array context above the AEAD layer).
findings.fix_now_action: Add a `content_length: u32` (or `expected_recipes: u32`) field to DropBundle that IS bound by the envelope-sig (do NOT zero it in build_envelope_message). Verify at parse_cbor_bytes / consume_offline that `self.content.len() as u32 == self.content_length`. Mint typed ErrorCode arm `E_DROP_BUNDLE_CONTENT_TRUNCATED` + add test pin `tf3f_drop_bundle_inter_recipe_truncation_fails`. This is a wire-format change (new field) — must coordinate with G-CORE-9 freeze gate; if post-freeze the FIX-NOW destination is `V1-FROZEN-INTERFACE-DEFERRED.md` Row D-NEW per HARD RULE 12 clause-(b) with G-COMP-1 destination naming the field-mint + tag-bump, AND a Compromise entry in SECURITY-POSTURE.md documenting the asymmetry pre-fix.

findings.summary: AuthorizationGrant `audience_pubkey` is NOT in `binding_message` yet ucan_blobs_protocol ARM 2 uses it as the EndpointId comparison source — audience-binding bypass at the ALPN handler.
evidence: crates/benten-caps/src/authorization_grant.rs:267 — `audience_pubkey: Option<Vec<u8>>` field on AuthorizationGrant.

crates/benten-caps/src/authorization_grant.rs:395-420 — `binding_message` function concatenates `BINDING_SIG_DOMAIN || ucan_bytes || km_bytes || audience-CID-bytes || scope_len_u32_le || scope_bytes`. There is NO `audience_pubkey` segment — the bytes are not covered.

crates/benten-caps/src/authorization_grant.rs:359-365 — L3-r1-1 Bundle FP added `scope` to binding_message + bumped BINDING_SIG_DOMAIN v1→v2 explicitly because 'post-sign mutation of `scope` was undetected, admitting a scope-widening attack'. The IDENTICAL attack-class on `audience_pubkey` (post-sign mutation undetected) is NOT closed — L3's sibling found by L4 cross-check.

crates/benten-sync/src/ucan_blobs_protocol.rs:442-460 — ARM 2 reads `request.grant.audience_pubkey` (the mutable field) + parses it to 32-byte Ed25519 + compares against `connection_endpoint_id`. If audience_pubkey was mutated post-sign, the attacker's own pubkey appears as the 'audience' the connection EndpointId must match.

Attack reproducer: (i) attacker steals a grant signed for audience X; (ii) attacker mutates `grant.audience_pubkey` to attacker's own Ed25519 pubkey; (iii) attacker connects to the handler with their own EndpointId (= mutated audience_pubkey) → ARM 2 byte-equal check passes; (iv) ARM 5 binding-sig verify against `grant.audience_binding` (the Cid — IS covered by binding_message at L417) passes because audience_binding is unmutated and the binding_message doesn't reference audience_pubkey; (v) handler proceeds to ARM 6 + dispatch.
This is the L3 sibling-finding ('audience_pubkey same-attack-class as scope — both unsigned, post-mutable, NOT in binding_message') cross-confirmed at the L4 production consumer surface.
findings.fix_now_action: Extend `binding_message` to bind `audience_pubkey` as a 6th segment (length-prefixed u32 LE || audience_pubkey bytes; empty for None). Bump BINDING_SIG_DOMAIN v2→v3. Update L3-r1-1 closure narrative to note this is the same fix-class as scope. Add a test pin `tf3b_audience_pubkey_post_sign_mutation_rejected` mirroring `tf3b_scope_post_sign_mutation_rejected`.
